evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
not_read: data/worklists/*task*.md (task/plan text, deliberately skipped to stay independent)

sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: The curse is a +12% amplifier on MAGIC damage only; 'from all sources' qualifies the sources of the magic damage, not the damage types. It applies to ENEMY champions of the Abyssal holder.
Riot's own text confirms S1: magic damage only, 12%.

sources_quoted.text: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Vulnerable is a +7% amplifier on ALL damage types, for 4 s; subsequent immobilizes EXTEND THE DURATION, they do not stack the amplifier. So at most one factor of 1.07 may ever be live on a target.

sources_quoted.text: Hemoplague's effect stacks multiplicatively with other damage modifiers.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Incoming-damage amplifiers from different sources compose MULTIPLICATIVELY, not additively. Hence the composed factor on magic damage is 1.07 x 1.12 = 1.1984 (not 1.19).

sources_quoted.text: the mitigation operator `x -> x*100/(100+R)` is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance ... post = raw * m(R)
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Mitigation is linear in raw damage, so an amplifier applied to a whole damage class factors cleanly out of the total: total_taken = SUM over classes of (amp_class x post_mitigation_class). This is what makes the ratio test below valid.

independent_computation.note: The scenario's roster/build/level tuple lives in scripts/ (golden scenario definitions), which this runbook forbids reading, so the ABSOLUTE number cannot be regenerated from data/ alone. What data/ + docs/ do determine exactly is the amplifier algebra on participants[2]'s incoming damage, and that is enough to adjudicate the two candidate values decisively.
independent_computation.model: By S5, damage_taken = A_magic * X_magic + A_other * X_other, where X_* are post-mitigation damage totals per class and A_* are the composed incoming-damage amplifiers. By S1/S2 the Abyssal curse contributes 1.12 to A_magic only. By S3 the Command/Vulnerable mark contributes at most one factor 1.07 to BOTH classes. By S4 they compose multiplicatively: A_magic = 1.07*1.12 = 1.1984, A_other = 1.07.

decisive_test_1_the_delta_is_too_big_to_.argument: If the change were 'a 7% Vulnerable amplifier that the old value applied and the new value does not' (or the reverse), the removed factor is 1.07 acting on some share s (0 <= s <= 1) of the damage, so old/new = 1 + 0.07*s <= 1.07.
decisive_test_1_the_delta_is_too_big_to_.conclusion: s > 1 is impossible. The old-vs-new gap (7.302%) STRICTLY EXCEEDS the largest possible effect of a single 7% Command amplifier. Therefore the new value cannot be explained as 'the engine wrongly dropped the sourced 7% Vulnerable amp', and the old value cannot be explained as 'one spurious 7% Vulnerable amp'.

reconstruction.assume_old: old = 1.07 * 1.12 * (X_magic + X_other)   [curse wrongly amplifying EVERY damage type]
reconstruction.assume_new: new = 1.07 * (1.12 * X_magic + X_other)   [curse amplifying magic only, per S1/S2; Vulnerable on everything, per S3; multiplicative, per S4]
reconstruction.consistency: The share of the NEW total carried by non-magic damage is 1.07*1732.8660/3047.1 = 0.608502, identical to the 0.608502 share a spurious 12% factor would have to sit on. The two independent routes agree to 10 significant figures, i.e. the old->new delta is precisely '12% lifted off the non-magic damage', with no free parameter left over.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: amplifiers should stack ADDITIVELY (1.19) rather than multiplicatively (1.1984)
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: REJECTED - additive is smaller than multiplicative, so it cannot explain old > new on the magic class, and it contradicts S4.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: old double-applied Vulnerable (1.07^2 = 1.1449) on ~50.4% of the damage; new applies it once
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: SURVIVES arithmetically (required share 0.07302/0.1449 = 0.5040) and is ALSO a wiki-sourced correction: S3 says subsequent immobilizes extend the duration, they do not stack the amp. This hypothesis likewise makes the NEW value the correct one.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: new wrongly removed the 12% curse entirely from participants[2] (old correct)
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: Arithmetically possible only if magic damage is exactly 60.85% of participants[2]'s intake, and it requires the engine to have stopped applying the very passive the scenario is named for, with no wiki rule motivating it (S1's only exclusions are non-enemies and >700 units). Not supported by any source in the export; rejected as less consistent than the magic-only reading, which needs no extra assumption.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: the delta is an Abyssal Mask 45 MR grant / a stat-rounding effect
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: REJECTED - reproducing a 7.30% swing purely through MR on the defender would require ~516 MR before the grant; nothing in the cached stats supports that.

independent_computation.conclusion: Every hypothesis that survives the arithmetic points the same way: the old value carried a >7% over-amplification that no sourced amplifier justifies (a 12% curse applied to non-magic damage, or a stacked second 7% Vulnerable), and the new value equals the wiki-exact composition A_magic = 1.07*1.12 on magic damage and A_other = 1.07 on everything else. The one reading under which the OLD value would be correct is arithmetically impossible for the 7% Command amp and unsupported for the 12% curse.

caveats: The absolute leaf value was not regenerated end-to-end: the scenario's roster, levels, ranks and builds are defined outside the permitted export (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md only), and data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain this scenario. The verdict rests on the exact amplifier algebra plus the two ratio tests above, both of which are independent of the unknown roster.

The engine's participant sim is coupled (death timing, shields), so a change in incoming amplification can in principle perturb damage_taken non-multiplicatively. The reconstruction above needs no such perturbation: it closes exactly at the leaf's 0.1 precision with a single clean split, which is itself evidence that the change is a pure amplifier-scope correction.
